alt: Building a palindromic row of letters by choosing only its first half and mirroring each choice into the matching position on the other side; too short a row has no free position for a second letter, so it is impossible.

steps.caption: Choose: position 0 is set to a. Mirror it into position 5.
Choose: position 1 is set to a. Mirror it into position 4.
Choose: the innermost position, 2, is set to b so the row holds both letters. Mirror it into position 3.
Every mirrored pair matches, so the row reads the same forwards and backwards.
Choose: position 0 is set to a. Mirror it into position 4.
Choose: position 1 is set to a. Mirror it into position 3.
Choose: the innermost position, 2, is set to b so the row holds both letters. Mirror it into position 2.
Every mirrored pair matches, so the row reads the same forwards and backwards.
Length 2: with only 2 position(s), each one mirrored onto another, there is no position left over to hold a second letter. A palindrome this short can only repeat one letter throughout. Impossible.
